questions.stem: Ethanoic acid reacts with sodium carbonate to produce fizzing. What gas is produced, and how could you confirm its identity?

options.text: Hydrogen; test with a burning splint for a squeaky pop
Oxygen; test with a glowing splint that relights
Carbon dioxide; pass through limewater, which turns milky
Nitrogen; the gas will extinguish a burning splint

questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids react with carbonates to produce carbon dioxide, water, and a salt: 2CH₃COOH + Na₂CO₃ → 2CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂. The fizzing is caused by CO₂ gas, which turns limewater milky (Ca(OH)₂ + CO₂ → CaCO₃ + H₂O). This reaction is a standard test to confirm the presence of a carboxylic acid.

questions.stem: Ethanoic acid has a pH of about 3 in solution, while hydrochloric acid of the same concentration has a pH of about 1. What does this tell you about ethanoic acid?

options.text: Ethanoic acid is a strong acid that fully dissociates
Ethanoic acid is a weak acid that only partially dissociates, producing fewer H⁺ ions
Ethanoic acid is not really an acid
Hydrochloric acid is a weak acid

questions.explanation: At the same concentration, ethanoic acid has a higher pH (less acidic) than hydrochloric acid because it is a weak acid. Weak acids only partially dissociate in water — only a small fraction of ethanoic acid molecules release H⁺ ions at any time. Hydrochloric acid is a strong acid that fully dissociates, releasing all its H⁺ ions.

questions.stem: Vinegar (ethanoic acid solution) is used in cooking and as a household cleaner to remove limescale (calcium carbonate). What products form when vinegar reacts with limescale?

options.text: Calcium ethanoate, water, and carbon dioxide
Calcium oxide and ethanol
Calcium chloride and water
No reaction occurs because ethanoic acid is too weak

questions.explanation: Ethanoic acid reacts with calcium carbonate (limescale) like any acid reacts with a carbonate: 2CH₃COOH + CaCO₃ → (CH₃COO)₂Ca + H₂O + CO₂. Although ethanoic acid is weak, it still reacts with carbonates — just more slowly than a strong acid. This makes vinegar a safe, effective limescale remover.

questions.stem: The functional group of carboxylic acids is -COOH. A student writes the structural formula of methanoic acid as CH₃COOH. What is wrong?

options.text: Nothing is wrong; this is the correct formula
Methanoic acid has only one carbon, so its formula is HCOOH, not CH₃COOH (which is ethanoic acid)
The COOH group should be written as COH₂
Methanoic acid does not contain the -COOH group

questions.explanation: The prefix 'meth-' means one carbon atom. Methanoic acid has one carbon in total (the carbon in the -COOH group itself), so its formula is HCOOH. CH₃COOH is ethanoic acid ('eth-' = two carbons). This is a common error — students must count the carbon in the -COOH functional group as part of the total chain length.

questions.stem: Ethanoic acid reacts with magnesium ribbon. A student observes fizzing and the magnesium dissolves. What are the products of this reaction?

options.text: Magnesium ethanoate and oxygen
Magnesium oxide and ethanol
Magnesium ethanoate and hydrogen
Magnesium carbonate and water

questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids react with metals in the same way as mineral acids: acid + metal → salt + hydrogen. The equation is: 2CH₃COOH + Mg → (CH₃COO)₂Mg + H₂. The salt formed is magnesium ethanoate, and hydrogen gas causes the fizzing. The reaction is slower than with a strong acid like HCl because ethanoic acid is a weak acid.
